Backed by top investors, they're gearing up for commercial launches next year from their Lausanne base.

data.name: Config AI's FPGA Compiler Draws AI Hardware Debate
data.summary: Founders Inc. showcased Config AI’s compiler, which turns PyTorch or ONNX models into FPGA bitstreams in minutes, running a small model at 48,000 tokens per second and eyeing larger ones up to 700B parameters. FPGA specialist Adam Taylor dismissed claims it could replace GPUs for AI, citing gaps in memory bandwidth and power efficiency—NVIDIA’s H100 boasts 3.35 TB/s versus AMD’s Alveo U280 at 460 GB/s. Config AI co-founder Ayush Kumar welcomed discussion but called for respectful tones, as engineers debate if FPGAs suit edge tasks better than massive LLMs.

data.name: US Open-Weight Models Hit New Legal AI Highs with Post-Training
data.summary: Harvey Research and Baseten applied a specialized post-training method to four recent US open-weight models: Muse Spark Open, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, Beam 1.0, and Inkling 2 Small. Muse Spark Open reached 30.3% all-pass on the Legal Agent Benchmark, topping previous records and beating systems like GPT-6.2 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2. The models also showed gains on non-legal benchmarks and generalized to other legal tasks, proving post-training as a low-cost way to customize for high-stakes work like law and banking. Harvey announced the results on November 24, noting US models are now competitive on long legal tasks.
